name: Chad
tagline: Zakouma, and the lakes of Ounianga
summary: Zakouma brought its elephants back from four hundred and fifty to over six hundred, the Ennedi is a sandstone massif full of rock art and desert crocodiles, and the Ounianga lakes sit in the middle of the Sahara without a river feeding them.
when: November to March. Zakouma is at its best in March, when the game concentrates on the last water.

entries.caption: Zakouma
entries.description: One of Africa's great turnarounds: from four hundred and fifty elephants to over six hundred.
entries.subject: a large herd of elephants moving across floodplain in Zakouma

entries.caption: The Ennedi
entries.description: A sandstone massif eroded into arches, towers and canyons, with water at the bottom of them.
entries.subject: the Aloba arch standing over sand in the Ennedi massif

entries.caption: Buffalo in Thousands
entries.description: Zakouma's buffalo move in herds of over a thousand, and the Kordofan giraffe with them.
entries.subject: a dense herd of buffalo raising dust in Zakouma

entries.caption: Zakouma in March
entries.description: Everything concentrates on the last pans, and the birdlife with it — crowned crane in their thousands.
entries.subject: black crowned cranes gathered at a drying pan in Zakouma

entries.caption: Emi Koussi and the Tibesti
entries.description: A 3,415-metre volcano in the far north, the highest point in the Sahara.
entries.subject: the volcanic massif of the Tibesti rising from desert

entries.caption: None, and Guelta Instead
entries.description: No falls. What the Ennedi has is the Guelta d'Archei, a permanent gorge pool.
entries.subject: camels drinking at the Guelta d'Archei gorge pool

entries.caption: Lake Chad and the Ounianga Lakes
entries.description: A shrinking inland sea in the west, and eighteen lakes in the Sahara that no river feeds.
entries.subject: the blue and green lakes of Ounianga between dunes

entries.caption: Landlocked, and the Lake
entries.description: The beaches here are the shores of Lake Chad, worked by fishermen in reed boats.
entries.subject: reed fishing boats on the shore of Lake Chad

entries.caption: Gallery Forest on the Rivers
entries.description: The Chari and Logone carry woodland far north into the Sahel.
entries.subject: gallery forest along the Chari river in southern Chad

entries.caption: Crossing the Ennedi
entries.description: Ten days by four-wheel-drive between arches and gueltas, sleeping under the rock.
entries.subject: a desert camp under a sandstone arch in the Ennedi

entries.caption: Two Hundred Groups
entries.description: Toubou and Zaghawa in the north, Sara in the south, and Arabic and French across both.
entries.subject: a market crowd in N'Djamena

entries.caption: The Toubou
entries.description: A desert people of the Tibesti and Ennedi, and among the most self-sufficient anywhere.
entries.subject: a Toubou man beside camels in the Ennedi

entries.caption: Boule and Grilled Capitaine
entries.description: Millet boule with sauce, and Nile perch off the Chari grilled on the bank.
entries.subject: grilled capitaine fish and millet boule on a plate

entries.caption: The Gerewol and the Camel Races
entries.description: Wodaabe gatherings in the Sahel, and camel racing in the desert north.
entries.subject: camel racing at a gathering in the Chadian Sahel

entries.caption: Leatherwork and Silver
entries.description: Toubou leather, Sara basketry, and silver from the N'Djamena market.
entries.subject: tooled leather camel gear and silver at a Chadian market

entries.caption: Ennedi Rock Art
entries.description: Thousands of painted and engraved panels recording a Sahara with cattle and giraffe in it.
entries.subject: painted rock art figures of cattle on Ennedi sandstone

entries.caption: Two Sites in the Sahara
entries.description: The Ennedi massif and the Ounianga lakes, both World Heritage, both barely visited.
entries.subject: the layered sandstone towers of the Ennedi at sunset

entries.caption: N'Djamena
entries.description: A capital on the Chari, opposite Cameroon, with the largest market in the region.
entries.subject: the riverfront and low skyline of N'Djamena on the Chari

entries.caption: Mud and Banco
entries.description: Sahelian mud-brick in the towns, and reed and mat construction on the lake.
entries.subject: a mud-brick compound with a thatched granary in the Sahel

entries.caption: Tea in the Shade
entries.description: Three glasses, poured from a height, and no business concluded before the third.
entries.subject: men drinking tea in the shade of a wall in N'Djamena

entries.caption: Serious Country
entries.description: Distances are enormous and facilities are few. Zakouma is possible; the Ennedi is an expedition.
entries.subject: a vehicle on a long empty track across Chadian savanna

entries.caption: Walking Zakouma
entries.description: Zakouma allows walking with armed rangers, which very few West and Central African parks do.
entries.subject: a walking group with a ranger among trees in Zakouma

entries.caption: One Camp, and It Is Good
entries.description: Zakouma has a single seasonal camp. The Ennedi is tents you bring with you.
entries.subject: a seasonal tented camp under trees in Zakouma

entries.caption: The Turnaround at Zakouma
entries.description: African Parks took it on in 2010 after poaching had taken ninety per cent of the elephants.
entries.subject: a ranger patrol vehicle at dawn in Zakouma

entries.caption: Sandstone and Shadow
entries.description: The Ennedi arches in the last hour, when the sandstone goes from orange to red.
entries.subject: low sun through a sandstone arch in the Ennedi

entries.caption: The Guelta d'Archei
entries.description: Camels come down a gorge to drink, and desert crocodiles live in the pool below them.
entries.subject: camels descending to the dark water of the Guelta d'Archei

entries.caption: Why Chad
entries.description: A national park that came back from the dead, and a desert massif almost nobody has seen.
entries.subject: a lone vehicle beneath the vast sandstone towers of the Ennedi
